findings.title: Storage-denied cart: edits made on /cart never reach the memory cart, so /checkout shows and orders the stale cart
findings.failureScenario: The browser blocks storage (for example Chrome with all cookies blocked), so cartArea() returns null and readCart() returns the module-level memoryCart with persistent:false. The buyer adds A x1 and B x1 on the product page, which updates memoryCart through AddToCart's writeCart. On /cart they remove B and set A to 3. Because previous.persistent is false, the `&&` short-circuits and writeCart is never called, so memoryCart still holds [A x1, B x1]. The buyer presses «المتابعة لإتمام الطلب», a next/link client navigation that keeps module state. The checkout page's new CartProvider calls readCart() and gets [A x1, B x1], so the summary shows the removed line and the old quantity, and `create` orders them. The same thing happens after one setItem fails mid-session (quota): later edits are never written and the next page reads the older localStorage cart. This breaks DATA-AND-SECURITY 'Checkout transaction' step 1: 'Storage denial still permits session cart.'
findings.suggestedFix: In src/components/store/CartProvider.tsx, always write and keep the flag sticky: `const update = useCallback((next: CartV1) => { const saved = writeCart(next); setState((previous) => ({ cart: next, persistent: (previous?.persistent ?? true) && saved })) }, [])`. writeCart already updates memoryCart when storage is denied or throws. This also moves the side effect out of the state updater.
verifierCorrections: The suggested fix is correct and minimal for the storage-denied case: `const saved = writeCart(next); setState((previous) => ({ cart: next, persistent: (previous?.persistent ?? true) && saved }))`. It does not cover the mid-session quota failure the finding also names. There, cartArea() is non-null, so the next page's readCart reads the older localStorage value, not memoryCart. That case is practically unreachable for a tiny ID/quantity cart, so leave it or note it with a ponytail comment.

The suggested fix is correct for the storage-denied case: call writeCart(next) outside the updater on every update, and AND the result into a sticky flag. It only partly fixes the quota case: readCart (cart.ts:234-247) prefers localStorage whenever getItem works, so a cart that failed setItem is still read back stale on the next page. To close that too, have readCart return memoryCart when a write has failed in this tab (for example a module-level `writeFailed` flag set in writeCart's catch).

findings.title: One failed quote refresh replaces the whole checkout form, with no way to retry except a reload that loses the typed details
findings.failureScenario: The buyer types email, name, phone and address, then changes the city or applies a coupon. The debounced fetchQuote fails, from a mobile network blip or the 300-per-hour quote throttle (429). quoteFailed becomes true and the form unmounts, including the city select and the coupon input. The quote effect only reruns when [ready, cart, city, coupon] change, and nothing left on the page can change them, so the quote is never fetched again. The warning says «أعد المحاولة بعد لحظات», but the only way out is a reload. A reload keeps only the city and coupon (sessionStorage) and drops email, name, phone and address. The same thing happens when refreshQuote() fails after POLICY_CHANGED (lines 191-193).
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the form only when there has never been a quote: change line 377 to `if (quoteFailed && quote === null)`. When a quote already exists, show the same warning above the form and keep the form. The last quote is safe to submit because checkout_create re-prices and answers QUOTE_CHANGED with the fresh quote.
verifierCorrections: As suggested: `if (quoteFailed && quote === null)`, and render the warning inside the form (next to submitError) when a quote already exists, so the state stays visible. A stale quote is safe to submit because checkout_create re-prices and answers QUOTE_CHANGED with the fresh quote. Optionally add a retry button that calls refreshQuote() on the no-quote path, which is otherwise still a dead end.

findings.title: The order hold and cancel results are not announced, and focus is lost to <body> in the core checkout flow
findings.failureScenario:
A screen-reader user presses «تأكيد الطلب». On success, setPending swaps the whole
, including the focused submit button, for the hold view. Focus falls to , and neither the order number nor «حُجز طلبك لمدة 20 دقيقة…» is in a live region or focused, so nothing is announced. Pressing «إلغاء الطلب» removes that button as well: on success, focus is lost again and a

is inserted with its text already inside, which screen readers often skip. On failure, the error is inserted with role="note", which is not a live role, so it is never announced. This fails WCAG 4.1.3 and 2.4.3. The cart has the same pattern: its quote-failure warning (CartView.tsx:124) uses role="note", and line errors that appear after a quantity change (CartView.tsx:143-149) are not announced either.
findings.suggestedFix: In CheckoutForm.tsx, add a ref and tabIndex={-1} to the orderBox div and focus it in useEffect(() => orderBoxRef.current?.focus(), [pending, closed]). Change the role on line 361 from "note" to "alert". In CartView.tsx:124, use role="status" instead of "note".
verifierCorrections: Focus the orderBox (ref plus tabIndex={-1}) only after a user action, meaning a successful create or cancel, for example through a flag set in submit() and cancelOrder(). The suggested effect on [pending, closed] would also fire when pending is restored from readPendingOrder() on page load and steal focus there. Change line 361 to role="alert", and CartView.tsx:124 to role="status". Also cover the CartView line errors: keep one persistent role="status" region (or give each lineErrors <ul> role="alert") so errors that appear after a quantity change are announced, which the suggested fix leaves out.

findings.title: Cart and product quantity inputs cannot be cleared to type a new value
findings.failureScenario: In the cart, a line shows 3 and the buyer taps the field, presses backspace and types 5. The empty value is rejected, so React restores the controlled value '3'. The 5 then makes '35', which is also rejected, and the field stays 3. On the product page (AddToCart.tsx:39-42), clearing clamps to 1, so backspace then 5 gives 15, not 5. Keyboard and phone users can only change the quantity with select-all or the ± buttons.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep a local draft string for the input and commit a clamped value on blur or Enter. Alternatively, in both onChange handlers, return early without changing anything when event.target.value === '', so the field can be empty while typing, and clamp on blur.
verifierCorrections: The fix's alternative is wrong for CartView: returning early on '' is already what CartView does, and React still restores the controlled value. Keep a local string draft per input: set the draft on every change, commit when the draft parses to an integer from 1 to MAX_QUANTITY, and on blur (or Enter) clamp to [1, MAX_QUANTITY] and resync the draft. Apply the same to AddToCart.tsx.

findings.title: Hand-built signs beside Latin digits reorder in RTL: discount shows «50.00−», attention count shows «+200»
findings.evidence:
<dd>−{formatMoney(quote.discount)}</dd>
--- src/components/admin/AdminHome.tsx:194
? `${ATTENTION_CAP}+`
findings.failureScenario: In an RTL paragraph, U+2212 before the European-number run resolves to R (bidi rules W6/N1), so the discount row renders with the minus on the right of the Latin digits («ر.س 50.00−»). CLDR's ar-latn places it on the left through an LRM. On the owner home, «200+» resolves the trailing '+' to R and displays as «+200», which reads as "plus 200" instead of "200 or more".
findings.suggestedFix: CartView.tsx:276 and CheckoutForm.tsx:449: prefix an LRM, `<dd>{'‎−'}{formatMoney(quote.discount)}</dd>` (bidi rule W7 then makes the digits and the minus LTR). AdminHome.tsx:194: wrap the value in <bdi>…</bdi> or <span dir="ltr">.

For AdminHome, use `<span dir="ltr">` rather than a bare <bdi>: a bdi's dir=auto finds no strong character in «200+», so it is not a guaranteed LTR run. A root-cause alternative: formatMoney (src/lib/format.ts:61) emits '‎-' as its negative sign, and the rows call formatMoney(-quote.discount). That also fixes any future negative amount.

findings.title: The idempotency key lives only in memory, so after a lost response and a reload the buyer is blocked by their own hold and told to do something the page cannot do
findings.failureScenario: create reaches the server and the order commits, but the response is lost, so the UI shows «تعذّر الاتصال بالخدمة؛ أعد المحاولة.». The buyer reloads, which is a common reaction, and the ref-held key and fingerprint are gone. The next identical submit mints a new key. checkout_create finds the unexpired hold for this email or session and answers ACTIVE_HOLD. readPendingOrder() is null because the token never arrived, so the buyer sees «لديك طلب قيد الانتظار؛ أكمله أو ألغه أولًا.». The page offers no way to complete or cancel that order, and the buyer is blocked for up to 20 minutes. The DATA contract says same-request retries reuse the original order; with the key held only in memory, that stops working after a reload.
findings.suggestedFix: Persist the pair {fingerprint, idempotencyKey} with writeSessionValue under a new key in src/lib/cart.ts, and read it back in the mount effect. A reload-and-retry of the identical request then reuses the key, and the server returns the duplicate order with its access token.

findings.evidence: setSubmitError(error?.message ?? 'تعذّر إتمام الطلب.')
findings.failureScenario: The buyer types 'name@gmail.c'. The client regex /^[^@\s]+@[^@\s]+\.[^@\s]+$/ accepts it, but the server's EMAIL_SHAPE needs a TLD of at least 2 letters, so the function answers 422 {code:'INVALID', fields:{fieldErrors:{email:['بريد غير صالح.']}}}. CheckoutForm ignores fields.fieldErrors and shows the generic banner 'بيانات غير صالحة.'. The email field gets no aria-invalid or focus, so the buyer cannot tell what to fix. The same happens for a name over 120 characters (the input has no maxLength).
findings.suggestedFix: In CheckoutForm.submit, when `error?.code === 'INVALID'`, map `error.fields?.fieldErrors` keys that match the Field names (email, name, phone, address) into setErrors with their messages, and focus the first one, before falling back to setSubmitError.
verifierCorrections: Map error.fields.fieldErrors keys that are Field names into setErrors and focus the first one, as suggested. Also add maxLength={120} to the name input and tighten the client email regex to require a TLD of at least 2 characters, so the common cases are caught before the request.

findings.title: A duplicate `create` reply for an expired or cancelled order is shown as a live 20-minute hold
findings.failureScenario: The first `create` commits but the response is lost, so the form shows 'تعذّر الاتصال بالخدمة'. The buyer comes back 25 minutes later and presses «تأكيد الطلب» with the same fields, which reuses the same idempotency key. checkout_create answers duplicate:true with the order that checkout_expire has since marked 'expired'. The client never reads order.status, so it saves the pending order and shows 'حُجز طلبك لمدة 20 دقيقة', but the hold and its stock were already released.
findings.suggestedFix: In CheckoutForm.submit after parsing, if `order.status === 'expired' || order.status === 'cancelled'`, call setClosed(order.status) (and still set pending so the closed view renders) instead of presenting a live hold.
verifierCorrections: After orderSchema.parse, if order.status is 'expired' or 'cancelled', do not call writePendingOrder. Set pending, which the closed view needs, and call setClosed(order.status), so the stale token never reaches sessionStorage.

findings.title: Submit is not blocked while the quote is stale or refused, so avoidable refusals use up the buyer's five hourly create attempts
findings.evidence:
if (!quote || !cart || submitting) return
...
quoteHash: quote.quoteHash,
findings.failureScenario: (1) With a physical cart, the buyer picks a city and presses «تأكيد الطلب» before the 300 ms debounce and the quote round trip finish. create sends the new cityKey with the old city-less quoteHash. The server re-prices with the city and answers QUOTE_CHANGED «تغيّر السعر أو التوفر…», although nothing changed. (2) With quote.ok=false (OUT_OF_STOCK, COUPON_INVALID), the button stays enabled, and every press spends a Turnstile token and one attempt from the per-email throttle (5 per hour, taken at line 880 before re-pricing). After five presses, the buyer who then fixes the cart gets RATE_LIMITED for up to an hour.
findings.suggestedFix: In CheckoutForm.tsx, track a `quoting` flag: set it when the debounced quote effect schedules a fetch, clear it when the fetch settles, and disable the submit while it is true. In submit(), return early with setSubmitError('راجع ملخص الطلب أولًا.') when !quote.ok.
verifierCorrections: Don't call a synchronous setQuoting in the effect body: the code avoids that on purpose (react-hooks/set-state-in-effect, lines 90-91, 111). Instead, store the quote with the inputs that produced it: build `key = JSON.stringify([toApiLines(cart.lines), city, coupon])` in the effect and in refreshQuote, and call setQuote with that key. Treat the quote as stale when its key differs from the current one. Disable submit and return early when the quote is stale or `!quote.ok` (setSubmitError('راجع ملخص الطلب أولًا.')).

findings.title: CheckoutForm hand-rolls a copy of the shared `useTurnstile` hook
findings.failureScenario: No bug today. A fix to widget lifecycle or cleanup in useTurnstile (the hook the lib claims both forms share) would not reach checkout.
findings.suggestedFix: Use `const turnstile = useTurnstile('checkout')` in CheckoutForm.tsx (box/token/failed/reset/available). Replace the error-callback side effect with `useEffect(() => { if (turnstile.failed) setAwaitingToken(false) }, [turnstile.failed])`. Delete the local widgetId/token/turnstileFailed state and turnstileBox, and drop loadTurnstile/TURNSTILE_LOOK/turnstileApi from the public exports if nothing else needs them.
verifierCorrections: Use `const turnstile = useTurnstile('checkout')`, and call turnstile.reset() in the finally block. Don't use an effect to clear awaitingToken, because that would trip the set-state-in-effect lint. Derive the waiting state instead: `const waiting = awaitingToken && !turnstile.failed`, and use it in the button and in the requestSubmit effect. Remove the local widgetId, token and turnstileFailed state and turnstileBox. Stop exporting loadTurnstile, TURNSTILE_LOOK and turnstileApi only if nothing else imports them.

findings.title: quoteErrorMessage has no case for the dedication codes, so a dedication refusal reads «تحقق من محتويات السلة.»
findings.evidence:
case 'EMPTY_CART':
      return 'سلتك فارغة.'
    default:
      return 'تحقق من محتويات السلة.'
findings.failureScenario: The owner turns a signed variant into a physical one while a buyer's stored line still carries a dedication. The quote returns DEDICATION_NOT_ALLOWED for that line, and the cart shows only 'تحقق من محتويات السلة.'. The line's dedication input is hidden, because a refused line has no quoteLine, so nothing tells the buyer the dedication is the cause. INVALID_DEDICATION (a pasted control character) gets the same generic text. The function's own REFUSALS map says 'تحقق من نص الإهداء.' for both codes, which the doc comment claims this switch mirrors.
findings.suggestedFix: Add to quoteErrorMessage in src/components/store/quote.ts: `case 'DEDICATION_NOT_ALLOWED': case 'INVALID_DEDICATION': return 'تحقق من نص الإهداء.'`.
verifierCorrections: Add the suggested case. Because the refused line hides the dedication field, the buyer can only remove the line, so the DEDICATION_NOT_ALLOWED text could also say that (for example «هذا الخيار لا يقبل إهداء؛ احذف السطر وأعد إضافته.»). This is optional: the minimum fix is to reuse the REFUSALS text.

findings.title: A failed cart write is kept in memory but never read back while localStorage is readable, so AddToCart reports an item added that the cart never shows
findings.failureScenario: localStorage is readable but setItem throws (QuotaExceededError). writeCart stores the new cart in memoryCart and returns false. AddToCart ignores that return value and shows «أُضيف إلى السلة». On /cart, readCart() finds a non-null area and returns the stored cart without the new line, with persistent=true. The item is gone, and the «السلة مؤقتة…» note never appears.
findings.suggestedFix: In src/lib/cart.ts, record a module-level `writeFailed = true` in writeCart's catch. In readCart, return { cart: memoryCart, persistent: false } when writeFailed is set, before reading storage.

findings.title: The dedication text is saved to localStorage on every keystroke and never cleared, against DATA step 1 and P07's 'persist cart IDs/qty only'
findings.evidence:
cart.ts:5-7: localStorage holds `anasaq:cart:v1` ... `{ "variantId": uuid, "quantity": 1..20, "dedication"?: string }`
cart.ts:72: return JSON.stringify({ version: 1, lines: cart.lines })
cart.ts:260: area.setItem(CART_STORAGE_KEY, serializeCart(cart))
CartView.tsx:198: onChange={(event) => update(setDedication(cart, line.variantId, event.target.value))}
DATA-AND-SECURITY.md:57: "Browser stores only variant IDs, quantities and cart schema version in localStorage."
findings.failureScenario: A buyer on a shared family or office computer types «إلى سارة، مع كل الحب» as a signed-copy dedication on /cart. Each keystroke is written to localStorage['anasaq:cart:v1']. The cart is deliberately kept after the hold is created (CheckoutForm: nothing settles before P08), so the text stays in the browser forever. The next person who opens /cart on that device sees it. The plan's contract allows only ids, quantities and the schema version in localStorage (DATA step 1, WORK-PACKAGES P07 line 93).
findings.suggestedFix: In src/lib/cart.ts, have serializeCart write lines without `dedication`. Keep dedications in sessionStorage under a new key `anasaq:dedications` ({variantId: text}), using the readSessionValue/writeSessionValue helpers the file already has. readCart merges them back. The feature is unchanged within the tab: the dedication survives a reload and the cart-to-checkout step, but is gone when the tab closes. Update the matching sentence in docs/operations.md (line 426).
verifierCorrections: First decide which side is authoritative. If the plan wins, apply the suggested sessionStorage split, and merge the dedications back in both readCart branches: the storage branch and the memoryCart fallback. Otherwise, amend DATA-AND-SECURITY.md step 1 and WORK-PACKAGES P07 to allow a bounded dedication in the cart. Either way, fix S06.2 in the same change.
